source.title: Fundamental limits of neural network sparsification: Evidence from catastrophic interpretability collapse
source.authors: Dip Roy; Rajiv Misra; S. K. Singh

record.file_problem: No apparent file problem; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses and cites the superposition hypothesis, but its experiments measure neuron death and specialization under activation sparsification, not feature overlap, representational geometry, feature competition, or any other behavior specified by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper says superposition predicts more multiplexing as active neurons are reduced, but does not measure whether features overlap or become nearly orthogonal. Its dead-neuron and specialization results are related to sparse feature representations but do not test any listed version. Rows below are recorded as none-version findings. Figure trajectories and MIG/MSE results do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper cites the superposition hypothesis to motivate its work but never measures it. It does not measure feature overlap, near-orthogonality, polysemanticity driven by capacity, multi-dimensional features, or the canonicity or stability of SAE features. Its measures are dead-neuron rates, mutual-information specialization counts of SAE neurons on a VAE's activations, MIG and MSE, all under Top-k or L1 activation sparsification of the SAE. These are neuron-survival measures of an SAE under imposed sparsity. They do not bear on any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors also claim the collapse is intrinsic to sparsification rather than to the algorithm, training length or threshold. They further claim global metrics (MIG, MSE) mask local interpretability collapse, and that severity scales with dataset complexity (1.8–2.2× more dead neurons on Shapes3D).
record.recipe_differences: The study uses activation sparsification and neuron-specialization/death measures in VAE-SAE hybrids on synthetic image datasets; it does not use the original toy-model feature-loss setup or measure superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported collapse differs by dataset (dSprites versus Shapes3D), sparsification method (Top-k versus L1), training duration, and the thresholds used to classify specialization and dead neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: Under Top-k (k 500→50) and L1 sparsification, the SAE dictionaries on the VAE-SAE hybrids accumulate many dead neurons: 34–63% (Top-k) and 42–91% (L1). Specialized-neuron counts fall, while MIG and MSE stay stable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Extreme activation sparsification of SAEs in VAE-SAE hybrids produces substantial dead and unspecialized dictionary neurons, with severity depending on dataset and method.

fits_no_version.finding: 100 extra epochs at k=50 do not revive dead neurons on dSprites (+0.3 pp) and only slightly on Shapes3D (−2.9 pp). Specialization changes in opposite directions by dataset.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Extended training at target sparsity does not restore dead SAE neurons in these hybrids.

fits_no_version.finding: Specialized counts and dead percentages shift strongly with the classification thresholds, but dead rates stay high across all thresholds tested.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The magnitude of measured SAE neuron death and specialization depends on the thresholds chosen.

record.problems: The study uses one architecture family and two synthetic datasets, and does not directly measure feature overlap, polysemanticity, or representational geometry. The paper contains conflicting specialization counts for dSprites Top-k at k=50 (Table 1 versus Table 2 and Section 4.2) and differing values for some threshold analyses versus the main results. The stated code and trained models are available on request, not via a reported public URL.
record.rows_left_out: Not included: per-seed figure trajectories and the MIG/MSE results, because they do not measure the claim versions or add a direct feature-geometry result. Related-paper findings cited in the paper are not the study's own results.

untested.parts: All of it: no feature-direction geometry, overlap, sparsity-dependent transition or regular geometry is measured.
All of it: no measurement of polysemanticity or of feature allocation by importance.
All of it: no test of non-capacity sources of polysemanticity.
All of it: no LLM is studied. The SAE is on a VAE encoder trained on synthetic images, and recovery of ground-truth sparse features is not evaluated against superposition.
All of it: dead or specialized neuron counts under forced sparsity do not test whether SAE features are complete, stable across seeds, or canonical.
All of it: feature dimensionality is not examined.

record.verdict_notes: The introduction invokes superposition, saying fewer active neurons should force more multiplexing, but no superposition or entanglement measure is reported. The paper has internal numeric inconsistencies in its specialization counts (Tables 1, 2 and 4) and misnumbered references (Shapes3D cited as [22], which is Gao et al.). Code is available on request only. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No measurement of feature directions, overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent geometric transitions, or regular geometry.
No test of polysemanticity, feature competition for capacity, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions while others share.
No test of whether polysemantic neurons arise through mechanisms other than capacity pressure.
No LLM study, measurement of features spread across neurons in real models, or test of feature recovery from an LLM with a dictionary.
No test of whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of a model's representation.
No test of whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional features.
